name: Deep-ITM Bull Call Spread (Synthetic Stock Proxy)
summary: A bull call spread where both strikes sit below the current price, so the trade is already at max profit if the stock merely holds still -- a capital-efficient stock substitute with defined risk.

legs.strike_rule: Long strike at 0.80-0.90 delta (roughly 5-10% below spot).
Short strike at 0.60-0.70 delta, still below spot. Width sized so debit is 70-85% of width.

max_profit: (width * 100) - debit, achieved if the underlying simply stays above the short strike
breakevens: long strike + net debit per share (usually well below spot)

greeks.delta: positive, ~+0.15 to +0.25 per 1-lot (both legs high delta, so the difference is modest)
greeks.gamma: negative -- a drop toward the strikes hurts increasingly fast
greeks.theta: positive (typically +$0.5 to +$2/day per 1-lot), since the position is net ITM

typical_dte: 45-90 DTE. Longer is better here because the whole point is that time decay works for you.
when_to_use: Strongly trending names where you want stock-like upside participation with a hard floor on loss and a fraction of the buying power. Best when IV rank is 20-50; extreme low IV makes the deep ITM leg's extrinsic tiny (good) but the credit on the short leg negligible.
entry_rules: Underlying in a confirmed uptrend: 20-EMA > 50-SMA > 200-SMA and price above all three.
Long strike delta >= 0.80, short strike delta between 0.60 and 0.72, both strikes below spot.
Net debit between 70% and 85% of width -- reward:reward ratio is intentionally low; the win rate is the edge.
Probability of profit (approximated as 1 - short strike delta... i.e. delta of short call) implies >= 65% chance of finishing above the short strike.
Extrinsic value of the long leg <= 2% of the strike (deep ITM options with fat extrinsic are a bad deal and carry the most early-assignment exposure on the short side).
DTE >= 45. Do not use this structure under 30 DTE.
Open interest >= 250 on both legs (deep ITM strikes are thinner; widen the liquidity tolerance but never skip it).
Never open across an earnings date without accepting a full-debit loss scenario.
management_rules: Take profit at 85% of max profit, or at 21 DTE if the position is profitable at all -- whichever comes first.
Stop: close if the underlying closes below the long strike, or if the spread mid drops to 50% of the debit.
Do not roll. If the trend breaks, this structure is simply wrong; exit and re-evaluate.
Re-enter a new, further-dated spread only after price reclaims the 20-EMA for two consecutive closes.
exit_rules: Close the entire spread by 21 DTE at the latest. The last three weeks add almost no profit and all of the assignment risk.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: the short call is ITM by design, so check extrinsic value daily. If short-leg extrinsic < $0.15, close the spread the same session.

DIVIDEND GUARD (critical for this structure): close the entire spread the session before any ex-dividend date whenever short-leg extrinsic < 1.5 * dividend. Deep ITM short calls on dividend payers are the single most commonly assigned option in the whole family.
Absolute backstop: no open position past 15:30 ET on expiration day, ever.
assignment_risk: High and structural -- the short call is ITM from day one. Early assignment happens around ex-dividend dates and whenever the short call's extrinsic decays below the dividend. Being assigned makes you short 100 shares per contract against a long call; economically covered, operationally unacceptable. This strategy must have its dividend calendar check automated or it should not be enabled.
buying_power: Net debit only (e.g., a $10-wide bought for $8.00 holds $800/contract) versus ~$5,000-$10,000 of buying power for the equivalent 100 shares.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM strikes quote wider. Require bid/ask <= 15% of mid per leg and always route as a single MLeg spread order so the exchange prices the package, not the legs.
common_mistakes: Ignoring the dividend calendar; using it on short DTE where there is no extrinsic cushion; treating the capped upside as if it were stock; picking a width so wide the debit approaches the width (paying 95% of width for 5% of upside).
zero_dte_notes: Do not use. At 0DTE a deep ITM vertical is a near-certain assignment event with essentially no premium to collect.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
